original_question: For the Bianchi type IX dynamical system, prove that the past attractor is exactly the Mixmaster attractor, rather than merely a subset of it.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, Problem P13: the open problem asking to show that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system coincides with the Mixmaster attractor, rather than merely being a subset of it. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the four load-bearing ingredients of P13: the Bianchi type IX dynamical system, its past attractor, the Mixmaster attractor, and the goal of proving equality rather than mere inclusion. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
missing_details: The paper states this as Problem P13 in Section 5.2 on cosmological singularities and spikes, so the question should be framed in that specific open-problem and asymptotic-singularity context. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

The surrounding discussion makes clear that the setting is spatially homogeneous Bianchi type IX cosmological dynamics in general relativity near the past or initial spacelike singularity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

The draft leaves the paper's exact identifier for the target set implicit: the Mixmaster attractor is referred to here as the Bianchi II variety. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

The motivating partial result is also implicit in the draft: Ringström had only shown that the past attractor lies in a subset associated with the vacuum Bianchi I and II sectors, and P13 asks for the stronger equality statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
refined_question: In the study of asymptotic spatially homogeneous Bianchi type IX cosmological dynamics in general relativity near the past spacelike singularity, prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system coincides with the Mixmaster attractor in the paper's sense, namely the Bianchi II variety, rather than merely being a subset thereof. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
equivalent_formulation: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system is exactly the Bianchi II variety, i.e. the paper's Mixmaster attractor. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
justification: The draft is already very close to the official formulation: Section 5.2 first recalls that existing rigorous work proves only a containment statement for the Bianchi IX past attractor and does not fully identify the attractor or settle the relevance of the Kasner map, and it then states Problem P13 with essentially the same equality-versus-subset contrast as your draft. The rewrite above only restores the paper's precise scope and its explicit name for the target set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))
